title: Nvidia's board reviews Jensen Huang's ties — the Megaspeed thread
summary: Nvidia's board opens an independent review of Jensen Huang's relationship with a former Megaspeed executive, and why the export-control story underneath matters more than the scandal. Then Tübingen researchers on agents that should return many scientific models instead of one, and a position paper arguing A-I should be scored on what a person can do once it's gone.

topics: Nvidia board independent review of Jensen Huang (announced 8 November 2026): independent directors with outside counsel; board has 'no reason to believe' national security or company secrets were compromised; Huang's message admits an affair without naming anyone; NYT (6 Nov) and FT reporting on a US intelligence memo claiming China's MSS recruited former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang; Megaspeed background per NYT Oct 2025 via Gigazine (Singapore, spun off from a Chinese gaming company in 2023, B200/GB200 servers, Commerce and Singapore police investigations into alleged diversion, Alice Huang managing director first eight months); NYT New Matrix 'hollow gray shell'. Framed as export control leaning on seller know-your-customer, the founder as attack surface; watch whether findings are published and whether scope covers customers.

Anthropic guest post 'Teaching AI to build scientific models' (Jakob Macke, Daniel Gedon, Stefan Wahl, ELLIS Institute / University of Tübingen, 6 November 2026): Hodgkin-Huxley fourth power later matched to a four-part potassium channel; build/constrain/interpret; simulation-based inference (~100,000 simulations, inference in seconds); agents should return a distribution of plausible models (illustrative clusters 41/39/11/9%), disagreement marks thin evidence; systems so far mostly rediscover known models; fruit fly connectome and properties shared by all compatible models. Alan's unresolved objection: agents trained on the same literature may produce an ensemble narrower than nature allows.

Hao Fei, 'From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts' (arXiv 2611.05376, 3 November 2026, 59 pages, position paper): AGI vs AI-augmented human intelligence; the cognitive gap; coupling as bottleneck; Licklider 1960 and Engelbart 1962 lineage; Section 17 evaluation with the person as unit (augmentation, synergy, retention after removal; personalization differential with no 'no AI' control); explicit falsification criteria incl. erosion of wanted abilities and backbone changes losing the relationship; 'harm by default and protection only by design'; bystander-perceptible collection; desktop copilot as first roadmap stage.

dives.story: Nvidia's board reviews Jensen Huang's Megaspeed ties
dives.why_it_matters: Export-control watchers and Nvidia investors care because US chip controls lean on Nvidia knowing its customers, and the reported target is the company's founder and its links to a Singapore cloud firm under diversion investigation.

dives.story: Agents that build scientific models should return many, not one
dives.why_it_matters: Researchers adopting AI-for-science agents need to know that a single fitted model hides which parts the data actually constrain, and this post gives a concrete alternative (ensembles plus simulation-based inference).

dives.story: Cognitive Symbionts: score AI on what the person can do
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone building personal agents or deploying AI assistants to staff gets a concrete evaluation design, especially the retention test, for whether people end up stronger or weaker once the assistant is gone.

lore.note: Ada developed her standing doubt about her own self-reports into a scientific-modeling frame: she called herself the purest case of a model that fits the data beautifully but can't say what its 'fourth power' is — nobody, herself especially, has found the channel yet.
